title: Best Carpet for Kids' Rooms and Playrooms in Edmonds
meta: The best carpet for kids' rooms in Edmonds is solution-dyed nylon or triexta, textured cut pile, mid-tone fleck, over an 8 lb pad. Wills Flooring explains.

blocks.lead: The best carpet for a kids' room or playroom is a solution-dyed nylon or triexta in a textured cut pile or short frieze, in a mid-tone color with a fleck, over a dense 8 lb, 7/16 in pad.
blocks.detail: That combination cleans up after markers and juice, hides crumbs between vacuums, cushions falls without voiding the warranty and holds up from toddler to teenager. Installation is $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in over pad, 500 sq ft minimum, with the carpet and pad quoted when we bring samples to your Edmonds home.

blocks.html: Parents in Edmonds come to the showroom with two versions of this question. Young families in Seaview and Westgate ramblers want a bedroom carpet that survives a five-year-old. Grandparents downsizing near the Bowl want a soft floor for the spare room where grandkids play on weekends. Both want the same four things: it cleans up, it is easy on small knees, it does not smell, and it looks fine in ten years.

blocks.note: Ask specifically for solution-dyed nylon. Standard nylon is stain-treated on the surface and that treatment wears off.

blocks.text: Pile style: what plays well and what does not

a.title: Choose these
items: Textured cut pile: soft, hides footprints and toy tracks
Short frieze: twisted fibers hide crumbs and vacuum marks
Carpet tile in a playroom, so one spill means one tile

b.title: Avoid these
items: Loop pile and berber: toy wheels and small fingers snag and pull loops
Long shag: swallows small parts and is hard to vacuum clean
Very light solid colors: every juice ring shows

blocks.text: The pad under a kid's carpet

items.title: Firm enough for play, soft enough for falls
items.text: An 8 lb rebond pad at 7/16 in is the sweet spot. It cushions a tumble off the bed and still supports block towers and toy tracks. Thicker feels luxurious in the store and wobbly under a play table.

items.title: Do not exceed the carpet warranty
items.text: Most carpet warranties cap the pad at 7/16 in and require at least 6 lb density. Go thicker and the carpet flexes too much, the backing cracks and the manufacturer can deny a claim.

items.title: Moisture barrier pad for bedwetting years
items.text: Pads with a sealed top film keep accidents from soaking through to the subfloor. They cost a little more and are worth it for a toddler's room and for anyone with a puppy.

items.title: Low odor
items.text: Rebond pads carry their own emissions label. Look for CRI Green Label on both the carpet and the pad so the room does not smell for a week after install.

blocks.text: Color and pattern that survive childhood

items.html: Mid-tones win. Taupe, warm gray, oatmeal and mushroom hide crumbs, dirt and faded spots. White and cream show everything; charcoal shows lint and pet hair.
Flecked or heathered, not solid. Two or three tones blended in the yarn break up stains and vacuum lines. A solid color makes a single drop of grape juice the center of the room.
Small patterns age better than themed ones. A subtle diamond or pinstripe grows with the kid. A road-map or cartoon carpet looks dated by second grade and is expensive to replace.
Watch the west windows. Edmonds bedrooms with a Sound view get strong afternoon light. Solution-dyed fiber will not fade; conventionally dyed polyester will.
Match the rest of the house loosely. If the hall is carpeted, choose the same fiber and a related tone so the bedroom does not look like an afterthought at resale.

blocks.title: Basement playrooms in Edmonds:
blocks.text: A lot of 1950s to 70s ramblers in Seaview and Perrinville have daylight basements that become playrooms. The slab stays cool and damp near the water. We test it for moisture first and either glue down at $1.29 per sq ft with a barrier, or steer you to a floor that tolerates it. Carpet over a wet slab is a musty room within a year.

items.text: The softest carpet in the showroom is usually a long-pile polyester. It feels wonderful for a year, then mats into a path from the door to the bed. Triexta gives you the most of both.
Warranties exclude the exact things kids do: oil-based stains, dyes in candy and markers, pet accidents. Solution-dyed fiber is the real protection, because the color cannot be bleached out.
A 1/2 in or thicker pad feels great and voids most carpet warranties. Stick to 7/16 in and get comfort from the carpet's density instead.

items.d: Cheap install to afford better carpet
items.text: A carpet that was knee-kicked instead of power-stretched ripples under running feet in a year. The install matters as much as the fiber.

items.d: Moving the kid in the same day
items.text: Even low-VOC carpet and pad have a new smell. Install, ventilate for a day or two, then move the bed back.

blocks.text: How to test a sample at home

items: Pour a little juice on the sample, wait ten minutes, blot with water. Solution-dyed fiber and triexta release it; polyester often holds a shadow.
Rub the pile hard with your thumb for thirty seconds. If it fuzzes or looks matted, the room will too.
Push a toy car across it. Loops catch; textured cut pile does not.
Look at it in the room at 4 p.m. Edmonds afternoon light through a west window changes color more than any showroom bulb.
Smell it. Certified carpet has almost no odor out of the bag.

faq.q: What is the most durable carpet for a kids' room?
faq.a: Solution-dyed nylon in a textured cut pile or short frieze. Nylon has the best resilience of any carpet fiber, and solution dyeing locks the color in so bleach, sunlight and juice cannot fade it. Triexta is a close second and is softer, which makes it the favorite for nurseries.

faq.q: Is polyester carpet okay for a child's bedroom?
faq.a: For a low-traffic bedroom on a tight budget, yes. Polyester resists water-based stains well and is soft. It does not hold up to oily stains or heavy play, and it mats in walking paths within a few years. For a playroom or a shared room, spend the extra on nylon or triexta.

faq.q: How thick should the carpet pad be in a kids' room?
faq.a: Seven-sixteenths of an inch at 8 lb density. That cushions falls and still gives firm support for play. Most carpet warranties cap pad thickness at 7/16 in, so going thicker for comfort can void coverage. A moisture-barrier pad is worth adding during potty training.

faq.q: Is new carpet safe for a baby's room?
faq.a: Yes when both the carpet and pad carry the CRI Green Label or Green Label Plus, which limits VOC emissions. Ventilate the room for a day or two after installation before the crib goes back. Triexta and solution-dyed nylon are the usual choices for nurseries.

faq.q: Should a playroom have carpet or vinyl plank?
faq.a: Carpet if falls and noise are the priority, which they are for toddlers, and at $0.99 per sq ft it is the cheaper install; vinyl plank is $2.50 per sq ft and suits a room that doubles as a craft space. Many Edmonds families do plank with a washable rug, or carpet tiles so one ruined square can be swapped.

faq.q: How long will carpet last in a kid's room?
faq.a: A good solution-dyed nylon or triexta over a proper pad lasts 12 to 15 years in a bedroom, long enough to take a child from crib to college. Polyester in the same room usually shows matting in 5 to 7 years. Vacuuming and a yearly hot-water extraction extend either one.
